nodes.label: src/api
nodes.why: Owns the single HTTP surface. Declares one route, binds a Calendar per request, and delegates immediately. No pricing logic lives here.

nodes.label: src/instruments
nodes.why: A registry keyed by instrument kind. Adding an instrument means registering a class here, not editing the engine.

nodes.label: src/pricing
nodes.why: The largest and most-edited module. Holds the engine, the curve cache, and the closed-form models. Most incidents start here.

nodes.label: src/calendars
nodes.why: Business-day and holiday logic. Small, stable, and depended on by everything that touches a date.

nodes.label: src/risk
nodes.why: Bumps and re-prices for greeks. Consumes the engine; the engine never imports risk.

nodes.label: src/io
nodes.why: Loads curves and vol surfaces from the market store at startup. The only module that reaches outside the process.

blocks.title: BEFORE YOU START
blocks.text: You need Python 3.11, Poetry 1.7+, and Docker. Two of the setup commands below failed during generation and are marked as such. That is the repo's current state, not a bug in this page.

stops.title: Five sentences
stops.lede: If you read nothing else, read these. The fifth is the only one this tool could not verify, and it says so.

claims.text: payments-core prices linear and option instruments behind a single HTTP endpoint.
Every request must carry a settlement date, an instrument spec, and a market snapshot, and the date is rejected if it is in the past.
Every response carries the discount factor used and the timestamp of the market snapshot it was priced against.
It depends on curve and vol-surface data loaded at start-up, and it refuses to start if a curve is missing.
It is not a booking system: nothing in this repo writes to a ledger.

blocks.title: WHY SENTENCE FIVE IS AMBER
blocks.text: An absence cannot be anchored to a line of code. The tool searched for ledger and persistence writes, found none, and reports that as inferred rather than dressing it up as verified. Every amber mark in this document means the same thing: plausible, unproven.

blocks.text: The suite is CPU-bound in src/pricing. On a laptop with fewer than 8 cores, expect 90 to 120 seconds. Anything beyond three minutes usually means the timescale container is not up and tests are falling back to retry timeouts.

stops.title: One request, end to end
stops.lede: POST /v1/price, from the route handler to the serialized response. Six hops, each one a real line range. This is the path to hold in your head. Almost everything else in the repo is reached from it.

steps.claim: The route binds a Calendar per request through a dependency, then does nothing but delegate three times.
Validation happens before any pricing code runs: a past settlement date is rejected at the schema boundary.
The factory maps a string kind to a registered class and raises rather than guessing when the kind is unknown.
steps.predict: The factory has built the instrument. Which file does the request touch next?

steps.claim: The settlement date is rolled forward to the next business day, with a hard ceiling that raises instead of looping forever.
steps.predict: The settlement date is now a business day. Where does pricing actually happen?

steps.claim: The engine discounts off the currency curve, then branches: options go through Black-76 with a surface lookup, everything else is a forward difference.
steps.predict: A price exists. Which file turns it into the response body?

steps.claim: Serialization rounds the present value to six decimals and the discount factor to eight before it leaves the process.

blocks.title: ONE THING TO WATCH
blocks.text: RollOverflow at roll.py:121 fires when a calendar is loaded empty: every day looks like a holiday, so the loop walks past MAX_ROLL_DAYS. It presents as a pricing error but the cause is upstream in src/io. Inferred from the code path; this tool did not reproduce it.

blocks.prompt: Put these five hops in the order they actually execute.
blocks.provenance: survey.json → call graph from src/api/app.py:63-66, resolved statically
blocks.explanation: Validation runs before the handler body. That is the one most people get wrong, because the code that triggers it is not visible in app.py at all. It happens in the pydantic model bound to the parameter.

blocks.prompt: RollOverflow is raised inside src/calendars/, but the empty calendar was built elsewhere. Which module constructs Calendar objects?
blocks.provenance: survey.json → call graph → Calendar instances constructed only in src/io/market_store.py
blocks.explanation: calendars/ raises it, but the only place a Calendar is constructed is the market store. An empty calendar makes every day a holiday, so the roll walks past its ceiling. The error surfaces three modules away from its cause.

stops.title: Conventions and gotchas
stops.lede: Everything on this page is inferred from patterns in the code and in review history. None of it is verified against a written standard, because no written standard exists in this repo. Treat it as a strong hint, not a rule.

blocks.title: THIS ENTIRE STOP IS UNVERIFIED
blocks.text: The most useful content is the least checkable. Rather than mixing it into the verified stops and diluting them, it is quarantined here and marked once, loudly.

claims.text: Errors are raised, never returned as sentinel values: six of six error paths in the trace raise a typed exception.
New instruments are added by registering a class, never by editing a branch in the engine.
Dates crossing a module boundary are already rolled; roll_forward is called once, at the API edge.
Anything reaching outside the process belongs in src/io, which is why it is the smallest module and stays that way.
